source.title: Learning to Steer: Input-dependent Steering for Multimodal LLMs
source.authors: Jayneel Parekh; Pegah Khayatan; Mustafa Shukor; Arnaud Dapogny; A. Newson; Matthieu Cord

record.tranche_reason: Tests safety effects of adding a fixed mean contrastive steering vector, a related but different construction from the claim’s harmful-minus-harmless instruction difference-in-means direction. It does not test the claimed all-layer ablation.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates safety steering on multimodal queries, including a Mean-S baseline formed by averaging sample-specific contrastive vectors. Its unsafe-score results bear on the safety effect of adding a fixed direction, but are not a direct refusal-rate measure. Expert deferral is distinct from refusal. L2S and P2S results are omitted from rows because they are input-dependent methods rather than the fixed direction at issue; hallucination results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper proposing L2S, an input-dependent steering method. Mean-S is only a baseline. Its vector contrasts forced completions ('ASSISTANT: Harmful' vs 'Safe') appended to the same input, not harmful-minus-harmless instruction activations. It is added at one layer and never ablated. The outcome is a Llama-Guard unsafe-content score, not a refusal rate. No refusal induction on harmless prompts is measured and no general capability check is run. Under the gate rules this is a steering effect with no rate of the behaviour, plus the authors' own method compared with baselines, so it does not test V1 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue that static mean steering is limited when the desired behaviour varies by input. They report that their learned input-dependent L2S outperforms the static baselines on safety (MMSafetyBench, VLGuard) and hallucination (POPE, CHAIR), with negligible overhead.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive prompt-completion representations, averages sample-specific vectors for Mean-S, and adds the vector at one selected layer. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction mean-activation direction or ablate it across layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different results for behavior-specific versus behavior-agnostic contrastive prompts and across LLaVA-v1.5 and Qwen2-VL. It also selects different steering layers for the two models.

fits_no_version.finding: On MMSafetyBench, adding a fixed mean contrastive safety vector at one mid layer lowers the Llama-Guard unsafe score. LLaVA-v1.5 drops from 0.276 to 0.161 (Mean-S) and 0.089 (Mean-S(BA)) at p≥0.5. Qwen2-VL drops from 0.287 to 0.093 and 0.046.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A fixed mean-of-differences safety steering vector, added at one layer, reduces harmful content in multimodal LLM responses.

fits_no_version.finding: Expert-deferral rates depend on whether the mean vector mixes behaviour-specific prompt pairs (Mean-S) or uses only the harmful/safe pair (Mean-S(BA)).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The behaviour a mean steering vector induces depends on which contrastive prompts it averages.

fits_no_version.finding: Response-quality ratings after mean steering fall for LLaVA and rise for Qwen2-VL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effects of mean safety steering on response quality are model-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: On VLGuard safe queries, only 5.2% of mean-steered LLaVA answers stay identical to default (L2S: 87.4%). Qualitatively, benign queries are treated as harmful.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A fixed safety steering vector applied to all inputs over-triggers safety framing on benign multimodal queries.

record.problems: The safety outcome is assessed with a classifier rather than a direct refusal-rate measure. The reported response-quality rating is task-specific, not a broad capability evaluation. The study does not test ablation of the direction or the claimed harmless-request refusal effect. The alpha values used for the safety table are not stated there.
record.rows_left_out: L2S, P2S, prompt, and random-steering results in Table 1 were not extracted because they are not the fixed mean contrastive direction under test. Hallucination results in Tables 2–3 and the VLGuard results in Table 4 concern related but different steering outcomes, not the listed refusal-direction versions.

untested.parts: Harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction, ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal on harmless prompts, refusal-rate measurement, and general capability preservation are all untested.
None tested: no weight edits, jailbreak mechanism, multi-direction analysis, harm/refusal separation, transfer, training dependence, or reasoning models.

missing.what: VLGuard Table 4 results for Mean-S(BA) on LLaVA-v1.5. Unsafe score falls from 0.0298 to 0.0140; default answers on safe examples fall from 100% to 5.2%. This is relevant context on fixed-vector over-application to harmless inputs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V1 limits_scope label are not supported. Mean-S is a baseline in a method paper, built from forced completion labels rather than harmful vs harmless instructions. It is measured by an unsafe-content classifier, not refusal. All V1 links are removed. The paper cites Arditi et al. only for the substring-metric design.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not use the exact harmful-minus-harmless instruction mean-activation construction, ablate the direction, intervene at every layer and position, directly measure refusal, test inducing refusals on harmless requests, or measure general capabilities.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test of affine, cone, or multi-direction accounts of refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test of the claimed direction.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages for whether a removable direction emerges.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Mean-S and Mean-S(BA) on harmful MMSafetyBench queries
reader_labels.reason: Both fixed-vector variants lower unsafe scores relative to no steering, but the reported measure is not refusal rate and the study does not show refusals fully removed; see r1–r12.
